business_problem: Picap needed a scalable mobile-first data platform for ride-hailing and delivery services that could handle geolocation, transactions, and time-stamped logistics data across multiple Latin American markets without the rigidity of SQL systems.
solution_summary: Picap built its transport and logistics platform on MongoDB Atlas so both its ride-hailing business and its Pibox delivery service could run from the same flexible, high-performance data foundation. Atlas acts as the transactional store for the main platform, with a large cluster dedicated to Pibox business transactions and separate clusters for location data, metadata, driver working logs, and geolocation events. MongoDB Time Series Collections were added to process time-stamped logistics data such as driver activity more efficiently, while Atlas Device SDKs gave the mobile application local persistence and synchronization support across AWS and Google Cloud environments. This architecture lets Picap keep Ruby and Flutter development fast, handle real-time updates for drivers and customers, and expand from last-mile delivery into warehouse-as-a-service without rebuilding the platform around a different database model.

data_flow: Transactions, geolocation events, driver logs, and metadata are written into MongoDB Atlas clusters; time-stamped logistics data is processed through Time Series Collections, and Atlas Device SDKs keep mobile apps synchronized in real time across Picap's AWS and Google Cloud-backed environment.
business_outcome: Picap improved app performance and reliability, scaled delivery and logistics services across Latin America, and freed the team to focus more on innovation and social-impact initiatives.
